newsitem.title: UK: T&N asbestos provisions hit year result.
newsitem.headline: T&N asbestos provisions hit year result.

text.p: Auto components maker T&N Plc reported a hefty loss on Wednesday as it booked in its ambitious plan, revealed three months ago, to break free from its past as the Turner & Newall asbestos firm.

The British-based company reported a pretax loss of 388 million pounds ($625 million) for last year, against a 120.1 million pound profit in 1995, after exceptional charges of 515 million pounds for provisions and an insurance policy against future asbestos claims.
This gave the group 441 million pounds of provisions and a further 500 million of insurance cover against any future claims for ill-effects caused by asbestos.
The effective dividend payout for the year was held at six pence despite a net loss per share of 75.4 pence due to the provisioning.

T&N's share price slipped 3-1/2 pence to 156-1/2 after the news, with dealers saying there was some disappointment that underlying profits before charges came in below best estimates at 95 million pounds, against forecasts of 78 to 105 million pounds.
"The figures are a bit disappointing compared with the more optimistic expectations," said one trader.

But some analysts were more optimistic. "I think people were a bit confused. They didn't really know what to make of the numbers," said sector specialist Robert Speed of brokers Henderson Crosthwaite.
"We think it was a very strong underlying trading performance...They have got the asbestos problems behind them and we continue to recommend the stock," he said.
Chairman Sir Colin Hope said the group was looking to restore its operating performance, where margins slipped last year.
Operating profits before the exceptional charges fell to 178 million pounds from 227 million in 1995 on sales down to 1.96 billion pounds from 2.092 billion.
After accounting for disposals, operating profits fell to 173 million pounds from 204 million on sales of 1.89 billion against 1.85 billion a year ago.

Operating margins contracted to 9.1 percent last year from 11 percent in 1995. T&N said this was due to a combination of the cost of job cuts, price pressure from car makers and destocking of finished products.
But Hope said rationalisation work including some job reductions was now under way to recover profitability.
"We already have in place new efficiency improvements, new (cost) reductions which ensure those margins will be coming back from now," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We believe that at the peak of the cycle the group should be able to achieve 12 percent plus (margins)...and certainly an average 10 percent over the cycle," he said.
T&N said it also expected to raise around 70 million pounds from the sale of peripheral businesses this year to help finance the asbestos provisions.
When it announced the provisions in December, it said it intended to create a fund to be built up over the next three years from free cash flow, external fund-raising and disposals.

Hope said on Wednesday all the non-core businesses had been identified but he did not feel rushed to build up the provisioning funds since it was still not certain that the full amount would be needed.
T&N was also pursuing its expansion plans with its long-running battle to take over German firm Kolbenschmidt .

Hope said he expected a Berlin appeals court to give it the formal go-ahead by Friday to take a 24.99 percent strategic stake in the piston maker and to launch a review into a ban imposed by the Federal Cartel Office on T&N taking a bigger stake.
"I think we are expecting the final ruling literally today or tomorrow," Hope told Reuters.
In a new twist, it was announced later on Wednesday that Rheinmetall planned to buy a separate 24.99 percent stake in Kolbenschmidt from Commerzbank with a view to taking control.
T&N declined to say whether the sale was a help or hindrance to its own ambitions. "We have no comment to make at this stage...Rheinmetall is of course a very good company," a spokeswoman said.
But industry sources said it was possible Rheinmetall was making the move as a secret ally in T&N's own strategy to combine its own pistons business with Kolbenschmidt's.

Analysts said it would not be surprising but they could not see immediately how the British firm and Rheinmetall strategies could fit together. "We are all a bit baffled," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
T&N holds options on the stake in Kolbenschmidt with Germany's Metallbank, priced at 17 marks a share.

The British firm also had an option to buy the Commerzbank stake but the bank refused to renew the option when it lapsed at the end of last year, after the German Cartel Office banned T&N from buying into Kolbenschmidt.
But T&N said it still retains title to half of any profits Commerzbank makes from selling the shares at over 14 marks a share.
